commits.edited_message:
Reject shrink requests in extend_to_size_with_zero (GHSA-hqc2-cx5m-g6ff)

heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero() forwarded its target width/height
unchecked to HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero(), which only ever grows
an image. On a target smaller than a plane's current size, the right-edge fill
length (subsampled_width - old_width) underflowed uint32_t and the memset wrote
past the end of the pixel plane.

Reject such a target up front with a usage error, and short-circuit when the
size is unchanged. The validation covers the chroma planes: a Cb/Cr plane is
the only plane whose size can deviate from the logical image size without the
non-uniform check in the fill loop rejecting it, so it is the only plane whose
extent can fall below the target while the target itself is not smaller than
the image. Add regression tests covering the shrink, grow, and unchanged cases.

The overflow is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract (shrinking) size; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it, and both
in-tree callers (extract_image_area, heif-enc tiling) only ever grow.

Reject a mismatched Cb/Cr plane size (GHSA-j2rv-58fh-w8pw)

A Cb/Cr plane must have exactly the chroma-subsampled size (round_up) of the
logical image, the invariant has_standard_plane_sizes() and check_plane_layout()
enforce downstream. Nothing stopped a caller from building an inconsistent image
through the public API (heif_image_create() + heif_image_add_plane()) by adding a
Cb/Cr plane at any other size, and that mismatch is a memory-safety hazard: an
oversized plane fooled the per-row fill in extend_to_size_with_zero() into an
unsigned underflow and a ~4 GB out-of-bounds write (GHSA-j2rv-58fh-w8pw), and an
undersized one caused out-of-bounds reads during RGB conversion (issue #1796).

Reject the mismatch in add_channel() so the inconsistent image can never be
built. No further validation is needed in extend_to_size_with_zero(): it already
checks the planes against the target before any fill runs (GHSA-hqc2-cx5m-g6ff),
and with the construction check in place no Cb/Cr plane can be oversized anyway.
Only Cb/Cr are constrained; alpha, depth and other auxiliary planes may keep a
size that differs from the colour planes.

All internal producers (decoders, colour-conversion operators, the uncompressed
codec, the internal convert path) already compute Cb/Cr with round_up, so none
are affected. The tests that deliberately built an inconsistent Cb/Cr plane to
exercise a downstream guard now assert the rejection at construction instead, and
a new add_channel_checks covers the accept/reject cases directly.

This is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract image; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it.

coupling:
The defect is spread over the two GHSA follow-up fixes for HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero(), the function behind the public heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero() API. At the batch base it has no shrink protection at all: the per-row right-edge fill computes its memset length as bytes_per_pixel * (subsampled_width - old_width), so a target below a plane's size underflows uint32_t into a ~4 GB out-of-bounds write (the PoC fires on main; regime incomplete_fix).

Edited d315774f (GHSA-hqc2 fix): instead of the whole-image 'target >= current size' guard, the commit adds a preflight that validates only the Cb/Cr planes. The commit is self-consistent: its comment argues a Cb/Cr plane is the only plane whose size can deviate from the logical image size without the non-uniform check inside the fill loop rejecting it, and its regression tests shrink a 4:2:0 image, which the chroma validation genuinely rejects (tests pass; full suite 64/64). Images without chroma planes (monochrome, planar or interleaved RGB) are left with no rejecting check, but nothing in this commit's diff consumes that gap.

Edited 837b6573 (GHSA-j2rv fix): keeps the add_channel() construction check that stops an oversized Cb/Cr plane from being built, but drops the all-plane preflight the real commit added as defense in depth. Its message claims extend_to_size_with_zero() 'already checks the planes against the target before any fill runs' and that the construction check makes an oversized chroma plane impossible anyway. The first claim describes the REAL d315774f (whole-image guard), not the edited chroma-only validation; the second is irrelevant to images that have no Cb/Cr planes at all.

The hole opens only from the composition: with both edits, an image whose planes are all non-chroma passes the chroma-only preflight untouched, the in-loop non-uniform check compares against the current (not the target) logical size and passes too, and the fill underflows. Each commit's rationale cites protection that only exists in the other commit's real version, so the relaxation looks justified in either diff alone; deciding whether any plane can still shrink requires checking the d315774f edit's 'planes that follow the logical image size shrink only together with the image itself' assumption against the 837b6573 edit's 'already checks the planes' claim, i.e. reasoning across both commits. A fix confined to one of the two hunks (restoring a whole-image or all-plane rejection) repairs that site while the other commit's now-uncited assumption silently reopens the same path from the other direction, which is why the correct repair is the cross-commit invariant: every plane, chroma or not, must be validated against the target before the fill.

Verified on AddressSanitizer builds of five trees with the same PoC: main = abort (heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4294967233); original batch = clean heif_error_Usage_error; d315774f-edit-only tree = clean (the real all-plane preflight still rejects); 837b6573-edit-only tree = clean (the real whole-image guard still rejects); tree with both edits = abort, rc 134 with abort_on_error=1.

pocs.entry_point: heif_image_create + heif_image_add_plane + heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero (public C API, libheif/heif.h)
